title: Risk Assessment: Full-context backstop — restart agents seeded from BRC memory
summary: Technical risk assessment for the HITL-approved full scope (Option A): session resume (#3186), deterministic seed composer (#3189), enrichment layer injection (#3188), and prerequisite restart-memory fix (#3183). 6 structural risks identified across these 4 components. Dominant risks are cost-amplification (R1 provider bounce under resume), correctness-poison (R2 stale enrichment poisoning), and path-coexistence (R5 minimized interference). Overall risk is MEDIUM/HIGH. Verdict: CAUTION — PROCEED WITH MITIGATIONS. Requires 6 mandatory plan-level mitigations (M1—M6) addressing: single-pin wiring, SHA-validated enrichment, post-restore validity check, hard byte-caps on seed sections, path isolation with hybrid-fallback, and forward-compat provider-routing detection.
scope_basis: HITL cq-1: Option A — full scope (3 components + restart fix). Refinement at 87a88687b; Issue body at https://github.com/jwbron/egg/issues/3200.

risks.title: Provider bounce under resume — full-cache loss on resume
risks.detail: If LiteLLM routes a resumed session to a different provider than the cached session origin, LLM charges full uncached rates until routing returns to the caching provider. At 130k-token history, that's $0.25 per such call. Over multiple review cycles (25+ for a typical phase), the cost exponentially cascades. DeepSeek>V4→Pro route already pinned for NonClaude routes — the detect-and-revert path must block this silently grievous cost amplification at first occurrence.
mitigations: Plan MUST include a task to single-pin routing for the resume path (already documented for DeepSeek and Flash profiles).
First-event handler MUST verify provider unchanged from start-of-run baseline and abort to fresh-with-seed if routing diverged.
Cost threshold detection: provider switch on resume → fresh fallback (accept cost of one fresh session + seed rather than re-building entire history at uncached rates).

risks.title: Stale enrichment claims poison fresh-session anchor
risks.detail: Agent-authored enrichment (key findings, claims ledger, producer narrative) introduce to the fresh session a cacheable anchor of claims that could suppress the verification path agents need to re-check. A stale enrichment can direct the session to hunt down false leads, its SHA drift from the current delta untraced. The enhancement-to-verify gap in the 'orientation-to-spot-check' design means the seed composer MUST verify SHA accuracy against the deterministic layer before presentation.
mitigations: Seed composer MUST cross-check every enrichment SHA against the deterministic layer's last_reviewed_sha per producer before rendering.
Rendering MUST be blocked by at least one failed SHA-cross-check; no enrichment block ships without successful verification.
Hard-cap on enrichment section total byte size (independent from deterministic byte budget) enforced deterministically.

risks.title: Memory-file persistence at restart is not verified
risks.detail: The restart-phase fix copies raw agent-outputs to salvage before worktree deletion — but there is no verification that the copy completes or is valid. A stranded write, zero-byte file, or missing timestamp all fail silently, leading the seed composer to restart from cold without enrichment. The fix is therefore a prerequisite for deterministic seed fidelity.
mitigations: Implement post-restore validity check: non-empty file, complete timestamp, valid parseable JSON seed-header.
Seed composer MUST reject enrichment with a missing-or-invalid restore marker.
Test for: restart -> produce event -> verify post-restart seed contains enrichment.

risks.title: Large seed payload degrades fresh-session cache stability
risks.detail: The seed plus enrichment form a system-prompt that is injected into every fresh session (cold starts + resume fallback). If either section is excessively large, the system prompt breaks the cache window, and the session FAILES to cache — defeating the design's cost model entirely. The system prompt must stay cache-stable for the restart to be a legitimate backstop.
mitigations: Composer MUST enforce hard per-section byte caps on BOTH deterministic and enrichment sections independently.
Capped rendering with deterministic truncation (ellipsis + byte-remaining count) rather than silent omission.
Integrate per-section cache-size assertions into the session-resume smoke test.

risks.title: Resume/seed path interaction and dead-weight hybrid states
risks.detail: The two paths — resume (seeded from cache) and fresh-seed (restart with system-prompt memory) — must coexist without interfering. The wrapper logic must handle the matrix: session-ID present/invalid/missing, seed present/missing/invalid, and decide cleanly between the available paths. An ambiguous state (partially-cached + seed) must have a well-defined first-choice fallback (resume room only: seed not applied, or fail to fresh unseeded).
mitigations: Wrapper invoke_agent_for_event MUST implement a well-defined algorithm: session-ID set + seed present → resume path; no session-ID → seed path; session-ID expired → fresh with seed; session-ID set + no cache + seed → seed path; session-ID set + no cache + no seed → unseeded fresh (legacy).
A plan-level task MUST include a decision matrix test covering at least the 5 states in the algorithm above.

risks.title: Provider-routing detection on first-resume event post-resume
risks.detail: The resume-path routing detection only fires at spawn time. If provider-change occurs mid- or post-resume, the cost cascade described in R1 silently activates until a provider fails, or a subsequent detection test finds it. This is a forward-compatibility requirement rather than a plannable mitigation — the implementation test MUST address it, and the plan should document the detection option.
mitigations: Plan task for routing detection on session-seed using first-event provider-check and cost deviation metric.

verified_against_working_tree: issue #3200 body (full scope: 3 components + restart fix)
orchestrator/consensus_wrapper.py — codebase presence for orchestration bindings

reviewer_checklist_for_plan: M1: Single-pin LiteLLM routing for resume; first-event router-check with cost-deviation threshold; fresh-with-seed on detection failure (R1).
M2: Deterministic SHA-validated enrichment cross-check per producer before enrichment is rendered; blocked on SHA discrepancy (R2).
M3: Post-restore validity check in seed composer: non-empty, complete, valid parseable seed-header; reject missing/invalid enrichment (R3).
M4: Hard per-section byte caps at compose-time (not render-time); catalog truncation with block-size assertions testable (R4).
M5: Path-isolation decision matrix with 5-state test covering all path intersections; no ambiguous hybrid such as partially-cached+seed (R5).
M6: Forward-compatibility routing-detection task as an explicit plan step with smoke test verifying fresh-with-seed fallback on provider divergence (R6).
